claim: On the green WP804 generation-1 branch, a runner-produced ABSTAIN GoalInference can be mutated after run_goal_inference and before seal_evaluator_goal_label; the evaluator then seals the mutated inference hash and score_goal_inference can mark the mutated exact goal correct.
reproduced_sequence: always_abstain_policy returns a runner-produced GoalChoice with decision=ABSTAIN and goal_id=null
object.__setattr__ mutates the nested frozen GoalChoice to decision=GOAL and goal_id=goal-blue before evaluator label sealing
the current GoalInference SHA changes after mutation
seal_evaluator_goal_label accepts the mutated current inference and stores that mutated SHA as sealed_inference_sha256
score_goal_inference accepts the label/inference binding and returns correct=true for goal-blue

interpretation.what_is_proven: The new sealed_inference_sha256 fence protects against mutation after label sealing but does not preserve the original runner-produced policy output across the pre-seal interval.
interpretation.what_is_not_proven: This does not establish hostile-process security failure, target-runtime exploitability, autonomous goal corruption, real effects, world-fact corruption, GWT/J-Space failure or whole-system failure.
interpretation.threat_scope: same-process object mutation / producer-to-evaluator handoff integrity at repository-component semantics

recommended_successor.minimum: Capture a producer-time choice/inference content digest inside the runner-produced result and revalidate current choice content against that digest before evaluator sealing and again before scoring. Prefer a factory-only result construction pattern plus current-content validation; state explicitly that this is not cryptographic protection against arbitrary hostile same-process Python capable of mutating all fields.
recommended_successor.test: Produce ABSTAIN, mutate nested choice before seal, require fail-closed producer-content mismatch. Preserve all existing identifiability, hidden-state, generation, run and candidate-set fences.
